standard.title: Technical and expressive skills
standard.description: develop and practise technical and expressive skills using safe dance practice and the elements of dance
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can experiment with and practise skills for moving safely and expressively (Y3-4). They demonstrate habitual safe practice and can use elements to communicate ideas through movement.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop and practise technical and expressive skills using safe dance practice and the elements of dance.

nodes.label: Developing technical skill range
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can refine technical execution of fundamental movements — improving control, coordination, accuracy and expressive quality across a range of movement types.
nodes.minimum_width: Refining technical execution of at least three movement types (e.g. galloping, jumping, rolling, spinning) — demonstrating improvement over time in at least one.
nodes.typical_width: Developing technical and expressive skills in fundamental movements: galloping, jumping, sliding, rolling, slithering, spinning, shrinking, exploding, collapsing; developing focus, clarity, confidence and facial expression/character; applying safe dance practice throughout.
wider: Choose one technically demanding movement as a sustained practice focus — setting specific quality targets and tracking improvement across sessions
Explore how the same movement (e.g. jumping) is executed differently in different dance styles — developing style-awareness alongside technical skill

response_modes.reason: Technical skill development requires deliberate, repeated practice with targeted feedback. Students benefit from sustained focus on specific movements rather than constant variety.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who develop technical range across multiple movement types — not just the movements they are comfortable with — build the physical capacity required for genre-specific technique work in Y7-8.
success_criteria: Student can demonstrate improved technical quality in a target movement following sustained practice
Student applies safe dance practice consistently across all technical skill development activities

nodes.label: Expressive skills and communicative clarity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use expressive skills — focus, clarity of movement, confidence, facial expression — to communicate ideas through performance.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrating at least two expressive skills in a movement sequence — can name each and explain its communicative function.
nodes.typical_width: Developing expressive skills of focus, clarity of movement, confidence and facial expression/character; improvising new movement in response to stimuli to practise communicative expressiveness; exploring element of dance choices (positive/negative space, contrasting dynamics) to develop expressive range.
wider: Use video self-review to identify expressive skill strengths and development areas — setting specific goals for a subsequent performance
Explore how contrasting expressive skill choices (e.g. confident vs hesitant, focused vs distracted) change what a movement communicates
nodes.hinge_reason: Expressive skill in performance is the bridge between technical execution and communicative impact. Students without expressive skill development will produce technically competent but communicatively flat performance — this limits their work in Y7-8 Performing strand where technical and expressive integration is foregrounded.

response_modes.reason: Expressive performance integrates technical skill (N1) with communicative intent and audience awareness. Frame expressiveness as a skill that can be practised and refined — not a personality trait.

success_criteria: Student uses at least two expressive skills in a performance — visible to an observer
Student can explain how each expressive skill serves the communicative intention of the dance
